answer: Arrival-spread gating admits identities only in staggered time slots, so a burst of new accounts lands outside any slot and waits. Each admitted slot must carry a distinct timing signature, and a sparrow of traffic arriving early or late flags the batch for delay. The gate then pads that slot with a fixed nectar delay before the next admission, forcing clones to spread across many slots instead of one ripple. An attacker pays one full slot interval per identity, so a thousand clones cost a thousand intervals of serialized waiting.
